To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the information seeking behavior of scientists is changing, and that the primary change is in the use of electronic information services and products.

(1) Scientists rely on the journal literature, monographs, pre-prints, attendance at conferences, and personal communication to keep abreast with developments in their fields; (2) Scientists rely on journals, monographs, and attendance at conference to support their research; (3) Scientists prefer access to journal articles, monographs, conference proceedings, and preprints in a print, not an electronic, form; (4) Scientists rely on electronic bibliographic databases, especially Chemical Abstracts;

the astronomers, chemists and physicists rely on the journal literature and the mathematicians also use monographs, preprint services, attendance at conferences and communication with other mathematicians.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the information seeking behavior of scientists at the University of Oklahom, and with the impact of electronic information on that behavior.
the information seeking behavior of scientists and the role of libraries and information centers in the electronic information environment.
how scientists use information and how they perceive their library and information resources and services.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
scientists are using the Internet and electronic information sources more than ever before and will use them even more in the future.
the scientists surveyed are using a wide variety of sources of information to support their research.
scientists, particularly those in the sciences, are in a period of transition from print-based to electronic-based information sources and that the library is a key player in this transition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the scientists in this study were not yet ready for the electronic library, but were moving toward it.
scientists, regardless of discipline, rely on a variety of sources for information, but the printed article is still the primary information source. (Contains 12 references.)
scientists in the four fields studied have not abandoned the print literature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
scientists are not abandoning their traditional sources for information, even though they are using electronic sources.
the library should continue to support its traditional role of providing the printed journal literature and access to electronic bibliographical databases.
scientists are still very much wedded to the printed journal article and the printed reference tool.
